PASSO 1: em português dizemos «eu gosto: STEP 1: in English we say «I like coffee» — I is the one doing the liking. In Spanish the logic runs the other way: it's as if the coffee pleases me. The thing that's liked is the subject of the verb, and the person who likes it is marked with a pronoun: «Me gusta el café» (literally, coffee pleases me). STEP 2: the pronouns are «me, te, le, nos, os, les»: me gusta (to me), te gusta (to you), le gusta (to him, her, usted), nos gusta (to us), os gusta (to you-all, Spain), les gusta (to them, ustedes). STEP 3: the verb agrees with the thing that's liked, not with the person who likes it: if it's one thing, «gusta»; if it's several, «gustan»: «Me gusta el cine» (I like the movies), «Me gustan los gatos» (I like cats). STEP 4: if what's liked is an action, the verb stays in the infinitive and «gustar» stays singular: «Me gusta cantar» (I like to sing), «Me gusta cantar y bailar» (I like to sing and dance). STEP 5: the article is required before the noun: «Me gusta el café», never «Me gusta café». STEP 6: to negate, «no» comes before the pronoun: «No me gusta el café». STEP 7: intensity goes after the verb: «Me gusta mucho» (I like it a lot), «Me gusta bastante» (I like it quite a bit), «No me gusta nada» (I don't like it at all). To say you love something, «Me encanta» (singular) and «Me encantan» (plural) are common. To say you hate it, «Odio» (regular, subject I) or «No soporto» (I can't stand). STEP 8: with people, «Me gusta Pablo» suggests romantic attraction. To say you like someone as a friend, say «Pablo me cae bien» (Pablo strikes me well / I get along with Pablo). For family and friends, use «Quiero mucho a mi abuela» (I love my grandmother dearly).
o sentido de «gostar» está em português,: The meaning of «to like» is the same as in English, but the sentence structure runs opposite directions. English «I like music» (subject: I) corresponds to Spanish «Me gusta la música» (subject: the music). The two most common wrong paths — treating «gustar» as if the liker were the subject («Yo gusto la música»), or inserting «de» as English «of» might suggest («Me gusta de música») — don't exist in Spanish: there's never a «de» after «gustar».

PASSO 1: para dizer de quem se trata, ac: STEP 1: to say whose liking it is, add «a» plus the person, and repeat the pronoun: «A Pablo le gusta el cine» (Pablo likes the movies), «A mis padres les gustan los museos» (my parents like museums). The «le» and «les» can never be dropped. STEP 2: to emphasize or compare, use «a mí, a ti, a él, a ella, a usted, a nosotros, a vosotros, a ellos, a ustedes» + the pronoun: «A mí me gusta, ¿y a ti?» (I like it, how about you?). STEP 3: to agree with something positive, say «A mí también» or «Yo también» (me too). To agree with something negative, say «A mí tampoco» or «Yo tampoco» (me neither). STEP 4: to disagree: «A mí sí» (when the other person said no) and «A mí no» (when the other person said yes). Examples: «—Me gusta el té. —A mí también.» (I like tea. —Me too.), «—No me gusta la lluvia. —A mí tampoco.» (I don't like rain. —Me neither.), «—No me gusta el cine. —A mí sí.» (I don't like the movies. —I do.). STEP 5: «también» is never used with a negative: you can't say «a mí también no». For a negative, use «tampoco». STEP 6: to express a preference, say «Prefiero X a Y»: «Prefiero el té al café» (I prefer tea to coffee; a + el = al). With a verb: «Prefiero leer a ver la tele» (I prefer reading to watching TV). STEP 7: to give an opinion, use «Me parece + adjective»: «Me parece interesante» (it seems interesting to me), «Me parecen caros» (they seem expensive — plural). Also «Creo que + sentence» and «Para mí…» (for me, …). STEP 8: to say how interesting something is to you, «Me interesa(n)» works just like «gustar»: «Me interesan los idiomas» (languages interest me).
em português, «eu também» e «eu também n: English «me too» and «me neither» are the standard responses. Spanish «yo también» and «yo tampoco» work the same way, but with «gustar» it's more natural to say «a mí también» and «a mí tampoco», because «a mí» echoes the pronoun «me» already in the sentence. To disagree, we use «a mí sí» and «a mí no», which in English comes out as something like «I do» and «I don't».

PASSO 1: para perguntar a um amigo: «¿Qu: STEP 1: to ask a friend: «¿Qué te gusta hacer?» (what do you like to do?), «¿Te gusta el cine?», «¿Qué música te gusta?». With «usted»: «¿Qué le gusta hacer?». STEP 2: to choose between two or more things, use «¿Cuál?» («which one») and «¿Cuáles?» («which ones»): «¿Cuál prefieres?», «¿Cuáles te gustan?». Before a noun, use «qué»: «¿Qué color prefieres?» (what color do you prefer?). STEP 3: «jugar a» + a game or sport: «Juego al fútbol» (I play soccer), «Jugamos a las cartas» (we play cards). «Tocar» + an instrument: «Toco la guitarra» (I play guitar), «Toca el piano» (he/she plays piano). You can't say «jugar la guitarra». STEP 4: «leer, ver series, salir con amigos, viajar, cocinar, ir al gimnasio, pasear» are free-time activities (to read, watch shows, go out with friends, travel, cook, go to the gym, go for a walk). STEP 5: false friends: «exquisito» means delicious, and a cake can be «exquisita»; to say something's odd or weird, use «raro» or «extraño». Watch out too for «divertido»: it covers both «fun» and «funny». STEP 6: a full answer keeps the dialogue going: «Me gusta mucho porque es relajante» (I like it a lot because it's relaxing). Add the reason with «porque».
em português também se «toca» um instrum: English «exquisite» and Spanish «exquisito» look like a direct match, but they aren't: English «exquisite» means finely made or refined, while Spanish «exquisito» simply means delicious — food, not craftsmanship. The word that actually means «odd, strange» in Spanish is «raro», which has no visual resemblance to any false-friend trap in English at all.
